subject: Re: Encord & Cerity Partners | Intro
text:
Hi Moritz,

As discussed, sharing a couple of posts that outline T-Mobile's thesis on physical AI and the work happening at the AI-RAN Innovation Center with Nokia, Ericsson, and NVIDIA:

  *
Why Physical AI Begins with Intelligent Networks<https://www.t-mobile.com/news/network/why-physical-ai-begins-with-intelligent-networks>
  *
NVIDIA, T-Mobile and Partners Integrate Physical AI Applications on AI-RAN-Ready Infrastructure<https://www.t-mobile.com/news/network/nvidia-t-mobile-and-partners-integrate-physical-ai-applications-on-ai-ran-ready-infrastructure>

T-Mobile is building an ecosystem of physical AI developers deploying vision AI agents on the edge network. Every one of these developers needs high-quality labeled data to train the models running at the edge, which piqued my interest in Encord given your traction with a lot of the partners and potential partners we've spoken with.

Appreciate you making the time for a brief introductory call. Let me come back in a few weeks with more developed thinking after I've had a chance to debrief with the Physical AI team.

Best,
Julian

• Audio & video transcription (clean verbatim, full verbatim, and timestamped formats)
• Transcription review and linguistic editing
• Multi-layer QA (terminology consistency, formatting, accuracy checks)
• AI-generated transcription post-editing and human refinement
• High-volume multilingual transcription projects across 260+ languages
• Fast turnaround workflows without compromising quality standards

Our linguists are experienced in handling sensitive, technical, and time-critical content, supported by structured QA processes aligned with ISO 17100 and ISO 9001 standards.

Regarding case studies, as mentioned, we are bound by NDAs with our clients and are unable to disclose specific project names or materials. subject: Re: Just Called - Private AI leaders Dinner in Bellevue
text:
1. What are you most excited about personally or professionally regarding
AI?

Professionally. Agentic engineering and verifiability: defining the right
abstractions for what the system should be, what must remain immutable
without human input, what should be able to be mutable & even
autoregenerated on demand or rebuilt, & how systems can be restructured
into composable task-oriented primitives where workflows/dataflows can
easily be created or restructured as needed, with AI in the loop, +
autogenerated UIs for humans in the loop.

2. What do you see as the biggest gap in AI implementations so far?
 1) The learning curve - because people presume that it understands
english, that you can build ad-hoc
 2) Most companies have already put robust automated verification systems
and automated operability, allowing hundreds of humans to push to prod
daily with automatic monitoring and rollback on regression. Much of what is
needed to make AI a net positive, and not a liability relies on this level
of engineering practice and discipline, and they aren't there without AI
let alone with AI. Since AI, like any automation amplifies outcomes, this
needs to be dialed in. Most engineers or companies don't even think this
way, let alone have it's practice dialed in for years, to be able to tweak
it in an AI context.
3) Organizational bureaucracy—the tax of middle management and
coordination—is the biggest bottleneck, not necessarily engineering. Thus
gains from AI without reshaping the organization is often minimal
4) Hype and FUD confusing things. People just wanting to "purchase" a
solution, rather than putting in the hard effort to make it work

3. Any dietary restrictions? We'll pass this along to the restaurant.
No.
